issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning is semantically wrong — warnings are not exceptions
issues.detail: The code does `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)`. PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass (and dask.array.core re-exports it as such). The author calls it a 'performance warning' in the docstring of the new test, but the test uses `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`. Either the call should be `warnings.warn(msg, PerformanceWarning)` (and the test should use `pytest.warns`), or — if hard-failing is the intent given the data-loss risk — it should raise a real exception class such as ValueError or a dedicated subclass. Using `raise` with a Warning class is a category error that confuses the contract: callers cannot tell whether the operation may proceed. The PR description itself asks 'Would an exception be appropriate here?' — which means the author has not decided. Decide before merging.

issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise` — dead code, signals an unstated invariant
issues.detail: Inside the `for ax, ...` loop the body does `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` followed by `break`. The break is unreachable. More importantly, this betrays that the author has not stated the loop invariant. Is the contract 'fail on the first misaligned axis' (in which case the break is dead), or 'collect all misalignments and report once' (in which case the raise is premature)? State the invariant in a comment and remove the dead statement.

issues.description: Boolean precedence bug risk: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0`
issues.detail: The expression `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` parses as `not ((nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw) == 0)` because `%` and `==` both bind tighter than `not`. That happens to be what's intended, but it is exactly the kind of expression a careful reader has to stop and re-derive. Write `if (nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw) != 0:` or `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw:`. Code-as-literature: the reader should not have to consult an operator-precedence table.

issues.description: Only axis 0's first chunk is audited; the invariant claim is weaker than the check
issues.detail: The check reads `if len(dw) >= 1: nominal_dask_chunk_size = dw[0]` and then tests `dw[0] % zw == 0`. `normalize_chunks` can return non-uniform chunk tuples (the last chunk is typically a remainder), and `auto` can produce different sizes per axis. Auditing only `dw[0]` per axis is an under-stated invariant: 'the first dask block on every axis is a multiple of the shard size on that axis'. State that, and justify why the remainder block is safe (it is, because the last block writes into a partial shard at the array edge — but say so in a comment). Otherwise a future reader will assume the check is stronger than it is.

issues.description: `safe_chunk_size` formula ignores broadcasting across axes and uses a suspicious `max(1, itemsize)`
issues.detail: The suggested config value is `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)`. (a) `z.dtype.itemsize` is 0 only for `object` / zero-width dtypes, where the byte size is not meaningful anyway; the `max(1, ...)` smells like guessing rather than stating an invariant. (b) `np.prod` on a tuple returns a numpy scalar; the f-string will embed `np.int64(...)` in user-facing config advice on some numpy versions. Cast to `int`. (c) The error message tells the user to set `array.chunk-size` to exactly the shard byte size, but the *check* is divisibility by shard size per axis — the smallest safe value and the recommended value should agree, and the relationship should be stated.

issues.description: Asymptotically-OK-practically-wasteful: `dask_write_chunks` computed unconditionally, then partly discarded in the region branch
issues.detail: In the region branch the code computes `dask_write_chunks` via `normalize_chunks(... previous_chunks=zarr_write_chunks)` and then immediately rebuilds chunks per axis with `new_blockdim(s, c, r)` using `dask_write_chunks` as the source `c`. But `new_blockdim` expects the *full-array* chunking on that axis, and `dask_write_chunks` is already keyed to `z.shape`, so this happens to work — but the previous code explicitly called `normalize_chunks(write_chunks, z.shape)` to make the contract obvious. Restate the contract in a comment: 'dask_write_chunks is the desired full-array chunking; we then carve out the region.' Otherwise the diff reads as if `old_chunks` was simply renamed.

issues.description: Test asserts only `chunksize` (first block), not the full chunk tuple — same under-statement as the production check
issues.detail: `assert all(c % s == 0 for c, s in zip(result.chunksize, zarr_shard_shape))` only checks the nominal block size on each axis. If the rechunk produced, say, `((12, 12, 1, ...),)` the assertion still passes for the leading element while the array might in fact have an interior non-shard-aligned block (it won't, given how `normalize_chunks` works, but the test does not establish that). Assert the full property: for every axis, every block *except possibly the last* is a multiple of the shard size, and the last block is `≤` shard size or aligned to array edge. That is the invariant the production code is supposed to guarantee.

issues.description: Missing literate comment: what `previous_chunks=zarr_write_chunks` actually buys you
issues.detail: The PR description explains the key insight — `auto_chunks` 'nearly always concatenates the previous_chunks argument', so passing the shard shape yields shard-multiple chunks. This insight belongs in a comment above the `normalize_chunks` call, not only in the PR description. A reader six months from now will see `previous_chunks=zarr_write_chunks` and wonder why the *shard* shape is being labeled 'previous'. One sentence resolves it.

issues.description: Variable naming: `zarr_write_chunks` vs `dask_write_chunks` vs `zarr_chunk_shape` vs `zarr_shard_shape` is a thicket
issues.detail: Within ~30 lines the code carries `zarr_write_chunks`, `dask_write_chunks`, `nominal_dask_chunk_size`, and `zw`/`dw`. The test file adds `zarr_chunk_shape` and `zarr_shard_shape`. The reader has to keep four near-synonyms straight. Consider `target_chunks` (what dask will rechunk to) and `shard_chunks` (the zarr write granularity); single-letter `zw`/`dw` in the loop body are fine if the outer names are unambiguous.

issues.description: Error message advises `array.chunk-size` in bytes but does not state the unit
issues.detail: `'array.chunk-size': {safe_chunk_size}` — the value is bytes, and the surrounding prose says 'the size in bytes', but the f-string interpolates a bare number. A reader who copy-pastes the suggestion and later sees `array.chunk-size: 7200` in their config will not remember whether dask's config accepts strings like `'100MB'` here. State the unit literally in the suggested code (`dask.config.set({'array.chunk-size': '7200B'})`) or add a one-line comment in the message clarifying that the int is bytes.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED, NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The algorithmic idea — pass the shard shape as `previous_chunks` to `normalize_chunks` so `auto_chunks` concatenates shard-multiples — is sound and well-motivated by the PR description, but the implementation under-states its own invariants and the safety mechanism is type-confused. The most serious issue is `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)`: a Warning is being raised as an exception, with dead `break` afterward, and the PR description itself admits the author has not decided whether this should be a warning or a hard error. The divisibility check audits only `dw[0]` per axis and asserts the same weak property in the test, while the surrounding code reads as if a stronger property were guaranteed. None of this is asymptotically wrong — the rechunking choice is correct in the common case — but the code is currently not literate enough for a reader to verify that, and the safety branch needs to commit to either warn-and-proceed or fail-fast with a real exception before merge.
